works.title: Two-Dimensional Membranes for High-Value Ion Separation from Seawater and Brines
institutions: Tianjin Municipal Engineering Design and Research Institute
works.abstract: Seawater and brines contain substantial inventories of high-value ions, yet their extraction is constrained by dilute targets, concentrated competitors and feed-dependent speciation. Two-dimensional (2D) membranes offer short, tunable pathways that can amplify subtle differences in ion size, hydration, charge, and coordination. This review integrates ionic properties and aqueous speciation with membrane structure to establish a mechanistic framework for ion selectivity in 2D nanochannels. It critically examines size exclusion, dehydration, electrostatic partitioning, chemical recognition, and coupled non-ideal transport and evaluates their relevance to Li, U, Cs, Sr, Rb, and other underexplored ions. Major membrane platforms, including graphene-based materials, MXenes, transition-metal dichalcogenides, 2D metal–organic and covalent organic frameworks, layered inorganic materials and heterolamellar composites, are compared in terms of channel architecture, chemical tunability, stability, and manufacturability. The available evidence indicates that selectivity is not an intrinsic property of a nominal pore or material class, but an operating-state response of the coupled ion–solvent–membrane–electrolyte system. Finally, this review critically examines rational membrane-design strategies, outstanding challenges and future research priorities to guide the development of high-performance 2D membranes for the selective separation of high-value ions.

works.title: Crystalline three-dimensional membranes enable chromatography-free purification of natural products
institutions: University of Science and Technology of China
works.abstract: Chromatographic purification of natural products is solvent intensive and energy-demanding and remains a major bottleneck in the sustainable production of pharmaceutical compounds. Here, we show that crystalline three-dimensional membranes enable chromatography-free purification of complex natural product mixtures by organic solvent nanofiltration. The rigid, nanomechanically robust channels of the membrane sustain continuous 6-day operation with commercial Taxus crude extracts, achieving ∼96% retention and fourfold enrichment of paclitaxel while allowing valuable precursors to permeate. The membranes exhibit high solvent permeance with negligible swelling, enabling stable molecular sieving in methanol across extended operation. Scalable fabrication via nanosphere-assembled interfacial polymerization produces continuous crystalline membranes over large areas. Life cycle assessment reveals nearly an order-of-magnitude reduction in carbon emissions compared with liquid chromatography. These results demonstrate a membrane platform that can replace chromatographic steps in natural product drug purification, offering a sustainable route for active pharmaceutical ingredient production.

works.title: Non-Monotonic Dependence of Ion Selectivity on Interfacial Polymerization Time in Nanofiltration Membranes
works.abstract: Abstract Polyamide nanofiltration (NF) membranes offer promising opportunities for resource recovery because their sub-nanometer selective layers provide intrinsic ion−ion selectivity. However, achieving sufficient monovalent/divalent separation, such as Li+/Mg2+, remains challenging because the polyamide (PA) structure formed during interfacial polymerization (IP) is heterogeneous and difficult to control. As a time-dependent process, IP enables reaction time to regulate the PA layer structure and ion transport. Here, we systematically investigate IP reaction times from 10 s to 5 min in polyamide NF membranes and show that monovalent/divalent ion selectivity exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on the reaction time, reaching a maximum separation factor of 30.5 at 0.5 min. Shorter reaction times increased water permeance and reduced ion rejection due to incomplete polymerization, whereas prolonged reaction decreased water permeance and MgCl2 rejection while increasing LiCl rejection. Membrane characterization revealed that these trends arise from coupled changes in the PA network density and charge distribution. The 0.5 min reaction produced a thin (32 nm) and densely cross-linked PA, favoring water transport and steric exclusion of Mg2+. In contrast, the 5 min reaction produced a substantially thicker (117 nm) and more open PA layer containing carboxylic groups throughout its depth, contributing to stronger electrostatic exclusion of LiCl. These findings establish the IP reaction time as an important parameter for tuning the structure and charge of PA membranes, enabling improved control of monovalent/divalent ion selectivity.

works.title: Organic Solvent Nanofiltration Properties of Silica-based Membranes Derived from Propyltrimethoxysilane and Bis(triethoxysilyl)ethane
works.journal: Journal of the Japan Petroleum Institute
institutions: Dept. of Chemical, Energy and Environmental Engineering, Kansai University
works.abstract: Membranes with a molecular weight cutoff of approximately 300 Da are very useful for organic solvent nanofiltration applications in the pharmaceutical industry, especially for recovery of active pharmaceutical ingredients. However, achieving such molecular weight cutoff values using polymeric membranes is challenging because most polymeric materials swell or deteriorate in organic solvents. In this study, we prepared propyl-functionalized silica (PrFS) membranes using propyltrimethoxysilane (PrTMS) and bis(triethoxysilyl)ethane (BTESE) as silica precursors. Compared with conventional templated PrFS membranes, the PrTMS–BTESE membranes exhibited higher organic solvent permeance with a high methyl orange (molecular weight: 327 Da) rejection, and did not require template removal. The membranes demonstrated excellent performance in N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone, with a permeance of up to 0.20 L m−2 h−1 bar−1 and a rejection of 89-99 % for methyl orange. Thermal treatment was critical in optimizing the membrane pore size, hydrophobicity, and separation performance. These findings highlight the potential of PrTMS–BTESE membranes for organic solvent nanofiltration. The membranes can have finely optimized properties for solvent-stable separation in pharmaceutical and chemical processes.

works.title: Janus Nanoporous Metal–Phenolic Nanosheet Membranes for Highly Efficient Osmotic Energy Harvesting
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Osmotic energy, harvested by reverse electrodialysis, is a huge and promising renewable power source. However, the implementation still remains a longstanding bottleneck due to the lack of high‐efficiency membranes with both remarkable ionic conductivity and high permselectivity. Here, we report a new membrane constructed by Janus nanoporous metal–phenolic nanosheets (Janus MPNs), which overcomes the intrinsic trade‐off between ion permeability and selectivity. The Janus MPNs prepared via a facile interface‐induced coordination assembly strategy feature an asymmetric bilayer architecture comprising a microporous domain containing ∼0.96 nm pores and a mesoporous domain containing ∼9.4 nm pores, with each domain approximately 10 nm thick. The assembled Janus MPNs membrane integrates interlayer 2D nanofluidic pathways with ordered intralayer 1D nanochannels, enabling ultrafast ion transport rates approximately 21 times those of membranes relying solely on interlamellar transport. More importantly, the intrinsic sub‐nanometer pores and abundant negative surface charges within the metal–phenolic framework enable high cation selectivity, yielding a cation transference number ( t + ) of ∼0.936. When applied in reverse electrodialysis, the Janus MPNs membrane delivers a power density of 22.1 W m −2 under a simulated sea/river salinity gradient, outperforming state‐of‐the‐art two dimensional (2D)‐material‐based membranes. This work establishes new scaffolds for membrane technology and osmotic energy harvesting.

works.title: Demonstrating a Membrane-Based Process for the Recovery of Key Nutrients from Anaerobic Digestate Solutions
works.abstract: Abstract This study demonstrates a two-staged membrane separation process for the selective recovery of two critical nutrientsNH4+ and K+from a nutrient-rich anaerobic digestate (AD) collected from a wastewater treatment plant. NH4+ and K+ are both critical for fertilizer synthesis, and their recovery from wastewater sources presents a sustainable route for nutrient production while simultaneously addressing the environmental issues associated with excessive nutrient loading (eutrophication) in local water streams. For this, a nutrient-rich real anaerobic digestate feed stock from a local municipal wastewater treatment plant was selected due to its high nutrient content: NH4+ (650−850 mg/L) and K+ (70−90 mg/L). The first separation stage focuses on separating nutrients from organic micropollutants using a surface-modified ionically crosslinked nanofiltration membrane. This stage produces a nutrient-rich (NH4+ and K+) permeate stream by achieving ≥80% NH4+ and K+ passage (1 − %rejection) and ∼95% organic pollutant (TOC) rejection. These membranes also effectively rejected multivalent cations, including Mg2+ (∼92%), Ca2+ (∼89%), and Fe (100%), and improved product quality. This membrane in the first stage also entirely retained the phosphorus (P) present in the AD in the retentate stream. For the second filtration stage, a synthetic solution containing NH4+, K+, and Na+ at concentrations representative of the Stage 1 permeate was used as the feed to evaluate selective NH4+/K+ separation. For this, a covalently crosslinked polyelectrolyte-modified membrane was used to demonstrate the partitioning of NH4+ and K+ in two separate streams. In summary, this study demonstrated the membrane-based nutrient recovery technologies for treating real AD matrices, extending their applicability beyond the synthetic matrices investigated in earlier studies.

works.title: Digital-Assisted Workflow for Organic Solvent Nanofiltration: Accelerating Process Development in Pharmaceutical Manufacturing
works.abstract: Abstract Organic solvents contribute more than 80% of total process mass intensity (PMI) in pharmaceutical manufacturing. Although organic solvent nanofiltration (OSN) diafiltration processes can improve sustainability, achieving high product yield typically requires large solvent volume to operate. Here, we present a digital-assisted workflow, built on the OSN Designer framework, that enables rapid screening of OSN process configurations to identify architectures that minimize solvent consumption while maintaining API recovery. The framework integrates a solution-diffusion transport model, film theory for concentration polarization, and non-steady-state mass balances, calibrated from crossflow experiments with compound A on the Borsig oNF-3 membrane in 2-methyltetrahydrofuran. Validated with average concordance correlation coefficient (ccc) of 0.72 across steady-state and dynamic operating regimes, the model was applied without recalibration to evaluate four process configurations. A two-stage membrane cascade with closed-loop permeate recycling achieved a process mass intensity (PMI) of 7.76─a 92.4% reduction relative to the single-stage constant-volume diafiltration baseline (PMI 101.5). The formalized four-phase workflow reduces experimental effort to approximately 3 weeks from more than 6–8 months and is directly transferable to other pharmaceutical OSN systems.

works.title: Aggregation-Mediated Solar-Optimized Hybrid Seawater Desalination for Sustainable Potable Water Production and Wastewater Management in Coastal Delta Regions
works.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
works.abstract: Freshwater scarcity remains one of the most pressing environmental challenges of the twenty-first century, particularly in coastal and delta regions where population growth, climate change, saltwater intrusion, water pollution, and increasing pressure on freshwater resources continue to threaten access to safe drinking water. Although conventional desalination technologies, including reverse osmosis (RO) and thermal distillation, have expanded freshwater production, their wider application is constrained by high energy consumption, membrane fouling, scaling, operational complexity, and environmental concerns associated with brine disposal and wastewater management. This chapter proposes an aggregation-mediated, solar-assisted hybrid desalination framework that integrates low-voltage ionic aggregation, gravity-driven phase separation, electro-assisted desalination, and membrane polishing to improve potable-water production. The proposed framework combines ion aggregation kinetics, electrophoretic transport, sedimentation behavior, and solar-energy performance analysis within a unified physicochemical approach. A system-level energy factor is incorporated to evaluate practical photovoltaic losses and their influence on desalination efficiency. The analysis suggests that aggregation-mediated pretreatment may reduce the salinity load entering membrane systems, thereby lowering energy demand, reducing membrane fouling, and supporting more efficient treatment of saline wastewater and concentrated brine. The framework is further evaluated for climate-sensitive delta regions, where decentralized renewable-energy-powered desalination can strengthen freshwater security while promoting responsible brine management and resource-efficient water use. Overall, the proposed approach represents a complementary treatment strategy rather than a replacement for existing desalination technologies. Future studies should emphasize pilot-scale validation, techno-economic assessment, long-term operational performance, environmental impact evaluation, and opportunities for resource recovery within sustainable wastewater and circular water-management systems.

works.title: Energy and Retentate Reuses in Reverse Osmosis Alone and in Hybrid Processes for Sea Water Remediation
works.journal: WSEAS TRANSACTIONS ON ENVIRONMENT AND DEVELOPMENT
works.abstract: The membranes are very important treatment way for seawater desalination due to low energy and costs. In this study; the effects of increasing retentates fluxes (6.0, 14.0, 19.0 and 23.0 l/m2.h), temperatures (25oC, 35oC and 45oC) and transmembrane pressures (8.0 bar, 14.0 bar, 22.0 bar and 27.0 bar) on the removal efficiencies of the alone and sequential hybrid reverse osmosis (RO) operations was investigated for salt and retentate recoveries from the sequential reactor system. The energy reuse yields were provided by taken into consideration the hybrid reverse osmosis process. In the RO alone and in hybrid RO processes elevated rejection yields (99.80% and 99.99%) was detected, respectively. In both treatment processes, the specific energy utilization was compared. For maximum Br-1, SO4-2, NO3-1, PO4—3 rejections (99.95%) the energy was minimized in the hybrid reverse osmosis proses. This process exhibited lower energy consumption. Retentate recycling from the hybrid sequential reverse osmosis to the inlet/feed of RO alone minimize the specific energy use. The steady-state operational conditions to minimize the energy amount were a water flux of 19.1 l/m2.h, a transmembrane pressure of 7.6 bar and a temperature of 32oC.

works.title: Teknologi Membran untuk Dealkoholisasi Wine: Metode dan Efektivitas
works.abstract: Membrane technology has emerged as a sustainable alternative for wine dealcoholization, replacing conventional thermal methods that risk damaging volatile compounds. This comprehensive review analyzes the effectiveness of membrane-based methods—such as reverse osmosis (RO), nanofiltration (NF), and pervaporation (PV)—in reducing ethanol content without compromising sensory integrity. Study results indicate that high-pressure RO (>40 bar) can reduce alcohol by up to 50%, yet it potentially removes 15-20% of low molecular weight aromatic compounds (esters, terpenes). NF demonstrates an advantage in preserving the wine's sensory characteristics but with a relatively moderate ethanol rejection rate. Pervaporation, utilizing hydrophobic membranes (e.g., PDMS), shows up to 90% efficiency in ethanol-water separation, but it is limited by operational costs and scalability. A key advantage of membrane technology lies in its 20-30% higher preservation of antioxidants (anthocyanins, tannins) compared to vacuum distillation methods. Fundamental issues identified include membrane fouling, operational pressure instability, and their impact on the wine's volatile components. However, challenges like membrane fouling and volatile loss remain hurdles, particularly for red wines with high matrix complexity. Recent studies recommend a hybrid RO-PV system to achieve alcohol levels of <0.5% vol. while retaining 85% of the original aroma profile. Future research should focus on developing modified ceramic membranes and optimizing cross-flow operational parameters for industrial applications.
